title: Free Make It Happen Office Printable
excerpt: A free Make It Happen printable for your desk or home office. Download the PDF, print it on cardstock, frame it, and hang the reminder right where motivation dips.
quick_answer: A make it happen printable is ready-to-print digital wall art with the phrase Make It Happen as its focal point, downloaded as a PDF and printed at home. Print it on matte cardstock at Actual Size, frame it in a standard 8x10, and hang it above your desk at eye level.
content:
You sit down at your desk, open your laptop, and there it is again: the blank wall staring back at you. Maybe there is a stray sticky note curling at the corner, a charging cable you keep meaning to hide, and above your monitor a whole lot of nothing. You have scrolled through wall art online, added a piece or two to a cart, and then closed the tab because fifteen or twenty dollars for a single print you are not even sure about starts to feel like a lot. Meanwhile the corner that is supposed to keep you focused and a little bit inspired just feels flat and unfinished. On the mornings you most need a push, a small nudge to actually start the hard thing instead of reorganizing your inbox again, the room gives you nothing back. You do not need a full redecorating project, a designer, or a bigger budget. You need one small piece of art that says the thing you keep forgetting to tell yourself.

## What is a make it happen printable, and where does it belong?

A make it happen printable is a ready-to-print piece of digital wall art with the phrase "Make It Happen" as its focal point, sized to fit a standard frame and delivered as a PDF you print at home. It belongs anywhere you need a quiet push toward action: above a home-office desk, tucked beside a monitor, on a gallery wall, or propped in a small frame on a bookshelf. Because it is an instant download rather than a shipped print, you can have it on your wall in the time it takes to run one page through your printer, no waiting on delivery and no return-if-you-hate-it gamble. The Biolex version uses clean, modern typography on a warm neutral background, so it reads as intentional decor rather than a motivational poster from a break room. Print one for your own desk to start the workday on purpose, and print a second copy for a friend, sibling, or coworker who is chasing something big this year. It costs you a sheet of paper.

## How do you print make it happen wall art so it looks framed-worthy?

Print it on heavier paper with your printer set to its best quality, and a free download will look every bit as polished as a store-bought print. Start by opening the PDF and setting the scale to 100 percent or "Actual Size" in the print dialog, never "Fit to Page," which quietly shrinks the margins and throws the proportions off. For the paper itself, reach for 60 to 80 lb matte cardstock instead of thin copy paper; the extra weight stops light from showing through, keeps the sheet from buckling inside the frame, and gives it a substantial, gallery feel in the hand. In your print settings, choose "High Quality" or "Best," and set the paper type to Matte or Presentation so the ink lands crisp and the color stays true. If your home printer struggles with edge-to-edge color, save the file to a flash drive and print it at a copy shop or a pharmacy photo counter for a dollar or two. Either way, let the ink dry for a few minutes before you slide it into a frame so nothing smudges.

## What size and frame should you choose for a make it happen print?

The safest choice is an 8 by 10 inch print in a standard frame, because it fills the wall nicely above a desk and fits frames you can find almost anywhere. That said, the right size depends entirely on where the print is headed. A small 5 by 7 suits a shelf or a tight cluster of prints, while an 11 by 14 makes a bolder statement over a couch, credenza, or a larger stretch of empty wall. Match the print to a frame you already own, or to one of these common ready-made sizes:

| Print size | Best spot | Frame to grab |
|---|---|---|
| 5 x 7 in | Desk shelf or gallery cluster | Small tabletop or wall frame |
| 8 x 10 in | Above a desk or monitor | Standard 8x10, the most common |
| 11 x 14 in | Statement wall, over furniture | 11x14, add a mat for polish |

A simple mat inside a slightly larger frame gives even a free print that curated, gallery finish, and neutral black, white, or natural-wood frames keep all the attention on the words. When in doubt, print a couple of sizes and hold them against the wall before you commit, paper is cheap and it saves you from a frame that turns out too small.

## Where should you hang a make it happen print in a home office?

Hang it where your eyes naturally land during the workday, which is usually just above your monitor or on the wall directly across from your desk at seated eye level. That puts the reminder in your line of sight at exactly the moments motivation dips, mid-afternoon, or right before a task you have been quietly avoiding all morning, without you having to go looking for it. When the print stands on its own, aim for the center of the art to sit around 57 to 60 inches from the floor, the standard gallery height that keeps it from floating too high. If your desk faces a window, hang the print on an adjacent wall instead, so glare does not wash out the type or make you squint through the afternoon. Renters can skip the nail holes entirely and hang a lightweight framed print with a couple of removable wall strips that peel off clean when you move. The goal is simple: put the words somewhere you genuinely cannot miss them, so the message keeps doing its job on the days you need it most.

## How do you build a motivational gallery wall around it?

Pair your make it happen print with two to four other pieces that share a color and a mood, and one motivational print quickly becomes a gallery wall that anchors your whole office. Start by laying all the prints on the floor and shuffling them around until the spacing feels balanced, usually about 2 to 3 inches between frames. Mix a quote print with an abstract shape and a small line drawing so the wall has visual rhythm instead of reading like a row of slogans stacked in a line. A set of matching thin-profile gallery frames in a single finish instantly makes a handful of mismatched free printables look like a collection someone curated on purpose, and it is the one upgrade that does the most for the least money. Keep the palette tight: warm neutrals, one accent color, and plenty of breathing room around each frame. For more phrases to fill out the wall, browse our [free printable office wall art and quotes](/blog/printable-quotes-for-office-wall) and this roundup of [free motivational printable wall art](/blog/motivational-wall-art-printable) to mix, match, and swap out with the seasons.

## Why does a make it happen print actually help you stay focused?

A visible reminder works because it turns an intention you have to remember into a cue you simply see, and seen cues are far harder to ignore than the ones living in your head. Behavior researchers call this an environmental trigger: when the prompt to act lives in your physical space instead of your memory, you act on it more consistently, because there is nothing to recall in the first place. A phrase like "make it happen," placed right where you work, quietly reframes the moment before a hard task, less "should I," more "I already decided." It will not do the work for you, but it lowers the friction of starting, which is almost always the hardest part of anything worth doing. There is a small ritual in it too: glancing up, reading the words, and taking the next step becomes a habit loop you repeat all day without thinking. Over weeks, that tiny nudge compounds into real momentum. That is the quiet power of a make it happen printable: it is cheap, it is fast, and it keeps working in the background long after you have stopped noticing it hanging there. Print it, frame it, and hang it where you cannot miss it, then let a few square inches of wall keep pulling you back to what matters.

Download it, print it tonight, and give tomorrow's you something worth looking up at.
